claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can be maintained as a single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloy in the stated high-temperature regime.
Equilibrium chemical short-range order can form at high temperature in refractory high-entropy alloys.
SRO clusters in HfNbTaTiZr can form a percolating network.
Cooling rate or annealing temperature can tune SRO from isolated clusters to a percolating network while retaining the single-phase bcc structure.
SRO is stable above 800 K in the proposed HfNbTaTiZr system.
Percolating SRO produces a spatially correlated force-constant-disorder field.
Lattice thermal conductivity dominates heat transport in the refractory bcc alloys under consideration.
Standard point-defect transport models assume uncorrelated disorder.
Force-constant mismatch between SRO-rich regions and the random matrix creates strong phonon-scattering centers.
Phonons are strongly scattered both at SRO-cluster boundaries and within the clusters.
Once SRO clusters percolate, they create a continuous high-scattering network that behaves as a phonon glass within the crystal.
The conductivity response scales with percolation probability rather than linearly with defect concentration.
Crossing the SRO percolation threshold causes an abrupt, nonlinear reduction in lattice thermal conductivity.
The reduction in lattice thermal conductivity exceeds that predicted by serial/parallel mixing or simple point-defect-scattering models.
The measured lattice thermal conductivity will be more than 20% below predictions from Wiedemann-Franz-law or Matthiessen-rule models.
The exact percolation threshold varies with atomic-size mismatch and bonding characteristics.
The magnitude of the conductivity drop depends on the force-constant contrast between SRO-rich and random regions.
APT or high-resolution TEM can quantify the SRO cluster-size distribution and connectivity needed to identify percolation.
A linear conductivity decrease without a transition at measured percolation, or persistently high conductivity after percolation, would falsify the hypothesis.
